svg.aria-label: Model auto-discovery, tier classification, admin policy routing and the health circuit breaker
svg.text: MODEL AUTO-DISCOVERY, ROUTING AND THE HEALTH BREAKER
The platform is not pinned to a model string in an env var. It discovers what exists, ranks it by policy, and demotes what misbehaves — at runtime.
1 · DISCOVERY — A LONG-LIVED IN-PROCESS SINGLETON
Anthropic /v1/models — on boot, then every 12 hours
Non-blocking: the service boots first and discovers ~5s later. 3 retries with backoff.
Classify → tier, flag beta, sort newest-first
TIER_PATTERNS fable → opus → sonnet → haiku (first match wins)
BETA_RE beta | preview | alpha | experimental | rc → admin opt-in only
Model ids are regex-validated before use — a malformed id never reaches the provider.
Persist the normalised catalog into Cosmos
So the admin dropdown renders without any browser ever calling Anthropic.
FAILURE POSTURE — SAFE DEFAULTS, NEVER THROW
First boot fails?
Catalog is empty → auto mode falls back to the manual priority list
(ANTHROPIC_MODEL_PREFERENCE → sonnet → haiku).
A later refresh fails?
The stale catalog is retained and the error is surfaced on the cached
snapshot — visible to admins, invisible to users.
The honest failure, recorded in the code itself
A model matching NO tier pattern lands in other, which auto mode never
selects. A new tier must be added to the pattern list and the tier order.
"…this is exactly how claude-fable-5 was missed." — source comment
2 · ROUTING — ADMIN POLICY DECIDES, NOT A HARDCODED STRING
AUTO mode
Walk the tier order, newest-first within tier:
fable → opus → sonnet → haiku
MANUAL mode
Admin-curated priority list, evaluated in order.
Excluded models are filtered out entirely.
Candidate list
Demoted models are pushed to the BACK,
not removed — degradation, not outage.
Attempt → retry → fall through
Per-model attempt budget, then the
next candidate. 60s per provider call.
The same resolver binds every Claude call in the platform
Interactive chat, Composer V2 dry-runs, and every scheduled agent run all resolve through resolveModelPolicy → buildModelCandidates.
One admin policy change moves the whole platform. There is no second place where a model id is chosen.
3 · HEALTH — A CIRCUIT BREAKER FED BY THE BUSIEST SURFACE
Observations come from CHAT
Chat hits the provider orders of magnitude more often
than weekly agents do. Per-attempt latency + outcome
are recorded per (model, attempt).
Thresholds come from ADMIN POLICY
p95 slow-latency · error-rate % · minimum sample
count · demotion minutes · breaker on/off —
all read from the group document per request.
Demotion, then automatic recovery
A misbehaving model drops to the back of the list for
N minutes, then returns. A snapshot is written to
Cosmos every ~60s so admins can see it.
Why an agent run does not drive the breaker: one scheduled report makes ONE provider call. A sample size of 1 cannot support a reliable demotion decision —
so agents consume the breaker's verdict but never write to it. Ownership of the feed sits with the surface that has the statistics.
Single-instance deployment is an explicit, documented assumption — there is no cross-instance state sync, and the code says so.
The point: model choice is operational configuration, not a deployment.
When a new frontier model ships, an admin picks it from a dropdown that populated itself. When one degrades, the platform routes around it and recovers on its own. Neither event needs an engineer.
